chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 8 of 21): the poet confesses bondage to courtesans who sell themselves and take a man's wealth, the frank pleasures of love, the begging of patrons with verse, and the body as a tree or hut that dies and is burned, and asks for teaching (போதகம்), a melting heart and the Lord's feet; the praise turns on Siva's matted hair and his dance, Sambandar's victories over the Jains, and the fire-column of Annamalai.
structure_note: The songs come in runs that share a metre and a closing line: 1097 to 1099 end அமரர்சிறை மீளவிட்ட பெருமாளே, 1100 and 1101 with the worlds' gods worshipping Kanda (அண்டர் அண்டம் தொழும்), 1102 and 1103 the vel sent from the hand, 1105 and 1106 காமவேள் மைத்துனப் பெருமாளே, 1107 and 1108 share their last two lines, as do 1109 and 1110. Confessions of women (1098 to 1104, 1107, 1108); the poet's trade of praising patrons (1105); quarrelsome disputants (1106); death and the pyre (1109, 1110); and 1097's body-tree and 1111's inner light.

1097.reading: The body is pictured as a great tree: rooted by the two kinds of deed in the soil and water of seven births, sprouting troubles, spreading maya as branches, desire as tender shoots and darkness as leaves, budding with loss and ripening the fruit of death; before its shade falls and it perishes in the heat, the poet asks Murugan for sweet teaching. The praise names him son of the fierce hero who struck down the moon, sun, gods, Indra, Brahma and Vishnu gathered at Daksha's sacrifice, rider of the peacock over the eight mountains who freed the gods from prison.
1097.nuance: The tree is worked out stage by stage (வேர், முளை, உலவை, குழை, இலை, நனை, பழம்), so that each phase of growth is a phase of ruin: the buds are loss (இழவு) and the ripe fruit is death (மரணம்). போதகம், teaching, is what the poet asks for here and in 1099. The Daksha lines name the gods at the sacrifice and an எதிர் வீர உக்ரர் who struck them, Siva in his fierce form.

1098.reading: The poet describes women who dress up and preen on the long street, beguile passers-by with their eyes, name a price for their breasts, coax them into their fine houses and onto flowered beds, and after love by Kama's rules melt the heart and take whatever wealth there is, and asks whether he must wander bound by desire for them. The praise names Murugan nephew of Krishna, who drank curd and ghee in the cowherds' homes and cried when Yasoda bound him to the mortar, bridegroom of the hunter girl, and the vel who won the Tamil debate by setting the palm leaf afloat against the flood.
1098.nuance: முலையை விலை கூறி விற்று and நிதியம் உளதே பறிக்கும் name the sale and the taking of money outright. மதனனுடை ஆகமம், 'Kama's scripture', makes the art of love a rival rule. The palm leaf sent up the river (ஏடு ... வருபுனலில் ஏறவிட்டு) in a Tamil debate is the story of Sambandar against the Jains at Madurai, and the song credits it to Murugan.

1099.reading: The poet tells how women with lotus faces and budding smiles embrace a man on the bed, give him their lips and say 'don't forget me; while body and life are one there is no yours and mine, I cannot bear a moment apart', and asks for teaching that will end the deceit of that union. The praise names Murugan nephew of the Mayan whose feet danced on the serpent's crowned, jewelled hoods, born in the Saravana pool, the peacock hero who circles the world-mountain, the six-faced one who is the life of the path of knowledge.
1099.nuance: The deceit is in the women's words of total union (உடல் உயிரதாய் இருக்க உனது எனது எனாமறிக்கை), which the poet quotes; தோதகம், fraud, is set against போதகம், teaching, in a rhyme. The dance on the serpent's hoods is Krishna's on Kaliya, told without naming him.

1100.reading: The poet calls himself a wicked thorn without merit, with a seething, loveless heart, who never comes to praise, carries the hollow where the five senses lurk, wanders seeking food, a stubborn, troubled wretch who is servant to women with kinsuka-red mouths, and asks when he will bow and praise Murugan's lotus feet with their anklets. The praise lists the Ganga, snakes, moon, lotus, thumbai and konrai in Siva's red matted hair, the green creeper at his side who bore Murugan, and names him the death of the clan of the cruel Jains, whom the worlds worship as the learned Kanda.
1100.nuance: The first half is almost all self-abuse, a run of nouns ending in -அன் (கண்டகன், பங்கிலன், அன்பிலன், சஞ்சலன், தொழும்பன், தழும்பன்). குண்டர் is the usual word for the Jains, so குலகாலா again points to Sambandar's victory credited to Murugan. Several words (அங்கதன், பண்டன், பொதும்பு) depend on how the syllables split.

1101.reading: The poet speaks of the life that shrinks on the day Death punishes, and of women who, seeking only money, offer refuge with sweet words while knowing their own deceit, measure their love and deal falsely, and asks whether he must wander joyless, with no love for Murugan, in desire for them. The praise names Siva, who came with love to break Sundarar's bonds and claim him as his servant, who wears thumbai, konrai, bones, the Ganga and the moon in his hair, and Murugan the Kanda of fitting words who delights devotees' hearts.
1101.nuance: தனந்தனை நாடி and இன்சொல் வஞ்சம் make the women's motive money and their means sweet speech. சுந்தரன் பந்தமுஞ் சிந்த வந்து ... தொண்டன் என்று அன்று கொண்டிடும் is the story of Siva claiming Sundarar as his servant at his wedding, the model of being taken into service. The run of syllables in the first lines is hard to split.

1102.reading: The poet describes lovemaking at length: drinking lips sweeter than the gods' nectar, the girdle loosed, falling into the pool of the navel, struggling on the bed with loveless women, breasts like golden pots, ornaments scattering, sword eyes reddening, sweat under the moon, and asks how a mind sunk in that sea of pleasure will ever reach the shore. The praise names Murugan the hero who married Devayanai, daughter given by Indra of the four-tusked white elephant and Puloma's daughter, and who sent the vel from his hand so that the sea, the mountain and the mango tree trembled and the gods were freed.
1102.nuance: The plea is a single question, எனவிதங் கரைசேர்வேன், 'how will I reach the shore', turning the sea of pleasure (இன்ப வாரி) into the sea of birth. அன்பொன்றிலாரொடு, 'with women who have no love', is the only judgement passed on the scene. The lines on the lotus-seated reciter of the Vedas are not clear to me.

1103.reading: The poet describes union with young women, flowers falling from their bee-haunted hair, cloth slipping, lips drunk, bodies entwined like anril birds until two hearts become one, and asks when Murugan will let him pass beyond the deeds those women bind him in and melt for him instead. The praise names him nephew of Vishnu who measured and swallowed the earth, bridegroom of Devayanai of Indra's golden city, who dwells in the hearts of those who love him and split Sura's body with the vel.
1103.nuance: The plea asks not for the melting to stop but for it to change object: உன்றன் மேல் உருக, 'to melt for you', answers the lovers' melting (அழிந்து) in the first half. The anril pair, a stock image of inseparable lovers, here describes the union the poet would leave.

1104.reading: The poet tells how he is undone by women whose breasts, red mouths, poison-dark eyes like Kama's arrows, dark hair and honeyed speech overwhelm him, and asks whether his senses, swinging to and fro, will never think of any way to go and rest without saying 'Om namo Kanda'. The praise names the fragrant trees of Valli's millet field, Murugan whose crown touched the cool feet of that faultless girl, and the teacher whom Siva with the goddess at his side worships.
1104.nuance: ஓநமோ கந்த என்று உரையாதே makes the failure a failure to say the mantra; ஊசலாடும் புலன், the swinging senses, is the image of the state. சீத பாதம் படுஞ் சேகரா has Murugan bowing his head to Valli's feet, the lover's humility, and தேவி பாகம் பொருந்து ஆதிநாதன் தொழுந் தேசிகா makes him Siva's preceptor. The list of trees in the praise is partly obscure to me.

1105.reading: The poet boasts that he is a poet who sings swift verse and kovai, crushes a crore of trash poets in debate, and asks whether he will ever give up standing before patrons, praising them as the rain cloud, the parijata tree and the Meru of giving, and saying 'listen' while he recites ornate and expansive verse. The praise names Vishnu on the serpent bed in the sea and Brahma, for whom Siva was a light beyond reach; Siva the death of Death; and Kama with his cane bow and fish flag who shot at Siva for Uma, whose cousin Murugan is.
1105.nuance: The poet names the kinds of verse he trades in (ஆசு, கோவை, சித்ர, வித்தாரம்), so his skill is the very thing he would give up. The patrons' praises (புயல், பாரிசாதத் தரு, த்யாக மேரு) are the stock hyperboles 1125 calls false. காமவேள் மைத்துனன: Kama is Vishnu's son and Murugan Vishnu's nephew.

1106.reading: The poet asks not to be worn down by dog-like disputants who call good words evil and argue the Vedas against those who come to real austerity, and asks Murugan, who rode the blue peacock and fought cruel Sura, to give him the true meaning so that he may lovingly chant his feet every day without fear. The praise names Vishnu on the serpent in the sea and Brahma, Siva who kicked Death's chest, and Kama, Murugan's cousin, whose flower arrows sank the chaste goddess in a sea of love.
1106.nuance: வேதர்க்கமிட்டு ஓயும் நாய் ஒப்பவர் compares sectarian disputants to dogs. நீதிப் பொருள், the righteous meaning, is set against their argument, and அச்சமற்று makes freedom from fear the fruit. The first lines' syntax is uncertain.

1107.reading: The poet lists the pleasures of concealing women, sleeping on their breasts, nail marks, the navel, the night's plunge into the great sea of delight and the nectar of their lips, and asks Murugan to end them all and give him the bliss of a mind dissolved in silence. The praise pictures Siva with the thousand-mouthed Ganga, hooded snakes, the moon, kura, vilva, konrai and other flowers in his long matted hair, and Murugan as the son given by the goddess who embraces him.
1107.nuance: மவுன ... மனோலய சுகம், the bliss of the mind's dissolution in silence, is a yogic goal set against the sea of sexual bliss (இன்ப ... மகோததி): one absorption is to replace the other. பஞ்சர between them is unclear to me (a cage, or Kama's five arrows).

1108.reading: The poet speaks of women whose sword eyes, sharper than the vel, war on young men's lives, who pretend love with deceit in their hearts and take great wealth, and asks not to whirl in their power but, knowing the nature that has no end and passing beyond misery, to have a mind to worship Murugan's feet. The praise names Siva, who drank the poison from the sea so Vishnu, Brahma, the Vedas and the gods might live, danced with ghouls in the fire, rode the bull and wears the snake, crescent and river, and Murugan the son of the goddess who embraces him.
1108.nuance: அளவி வந்து அணுகு மாநிதி கவர்ந்திடு மாதர: love is a pretence to take money. The last two lines repeat 1107's, so the two songs close as a pair.

1109.reading: The poet pictures the hut of the body full of disease and evil, children crying, wife and household, until Death's messenger comes and fate closes over his deeds, and asks that before his life is lost Murugan think of him with love so that he may praise him every day in the three Tamils. The praise names the vel that pierced the chests of the wicked Suras, the child of the dancer, Muruga of pure Tamil knowledge, coming on the peacock, who keeps his devotees like stored treasure and never changes.
1109.nuance: முத்தமிழினால் ஓத makes the praise he wants to sing Tamil praise, and the epithet சுத்த தமிழார் ஞான முருகோனே joins Tamil and knowledge in Murugan. வைத்த நிதி போல், 'like a hoarded treasure', is the image of how he keeps devotees, shared with 1110. Some lines (on the household, and the flower Brahma placed) are hard to construe.

1110.reading: The poet pictures his funeral: kin and children close by, women devoutly covering the body with silk and garlands, the bier lifted, the mourners calling and then plunging into the water to wash off their grief, the body burned; and asks that before his life departs Murugan give him a life of praising his golden feet every day with inner love. The praise names Murugan son of the three-eyed Mahadeva who is all things, the vel that dried the sea and killed Sura, who rides the peacock among men, gods and sages and keeps his devotees like stored treasure.
1110.nuance: The funeral is told from outside, as a sequence the dead man cannot see: silk, garland, bier, the plunge into water, and grief gone. The plea's timing, ஆவி பிரியாமுன், 'before life parts', is the book's common hour-of-death plea, here asking for a whole life of praise rather than rescue at the end.

1111.reading: The poet asks for an inner vision: a lotus that neither water nor earth touches, spreading in length and breadth as a form of light, joined with love like a flower and its fragrance, in a ground of light that sun and moon do not reach, where he may dance for joy that Murugan is the peacock's rider; he asks for the shining vel and the garland. The praise names the peacock whose dance shakes the thousand-hooded serpent and scatters gems like stars, the cock banner, and Murugan the child of the light of Arunai that Vishnu and Brahma searched for and could not find.
1111.nuance: சூரியனுடன் சோமன் நீழல் இவை அண்டாத சோதி, a light that sun and moon do not touch, is the language of yogic inner sight (as in the Tirumanthiram), here joined to bhakti: the vision ends in dancing. அருணஞ்சோதி points to the fire-column at Annamalai; who searched in the last line (ஆனைமுகவன், the elephant-faced one?) is unclear, and the whole song's syntax is uncertain.

links.note: Both follow the dead man to the pyre and the mourners' plunge into the water (நீர்த்தலை மூழ்குவர்; அலைநீரிற் புக்கு முழுகா). Tirumular calls the mourners people without justice, who forget once they have bathed; 1110 lets the bath end their grief and asks for a life of praise before that day.

The Thiruppugazh pictures the body as a tree whose roots are the two deeds (இருவினைகள் வேர்பிடித்து) in the soil of seven births, ripening the fruit of death, and asks for teaching before it falls. The Tirumanthiram names the same two, merit and sin (புண்ணிய பாவம் இரண்டு), and tells the knower to cut both at the root (வேர்அறத்) and seek the Lord beyond them. The song draws out the whole tree that grows from those roots; the Tirumanthiram verse says where the axe goes.

The Thiruppugazh shows women who price their breasts (முலையைவிலை கூறிவிற்று), lead a man into a fine house and onto a flowered bed (வடிவதிக வீடுபுக்கு மலரணையின் மீதிருத்தி), melt his heart and seize what wealth there is. The Kural says the false embrace of women who sell themselves (பொருட்பெண்டிர் பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம்) is like embracing a stranger's corpse in a dark room. Both say the paid embrace is empty; the song gives the setting the women stage, and the Kural replaces the bright room and flowered bed with a dark room and a corpse.

In the Thiruppugazh the women tell their lover that while body and life are one there is no yours and mine (உடலுயிரதாயிருக்க உனதெனதெனாமறிக்கை), and the poet calls this a deceit (தோதகம்) and asks for teaching to end it. The Kural's lover says sincerely that his bond with the girl is that of body and life (உடம்பொடு உயிரிடை என்னமற் றன்ன). The same figure of body and life is a vow of love in the Kural and a seller's line in the song.

The Thiruppugazh's women swear they cannot bear to be apart for a moment (ஒருபொழுதொணாது), and the poet names their union a deceit. The Naladiyar recalls the woman who said, like the anril birds, 'we will never part from you' (நித்தலும் நம்மைப் பிரியலம்) and then turned away like a ram's horn. Both treat the paid woman's vow of never parting as the snare itself.

The Thiruppugazh speaks of women who seek only money (தனந்தனை நாடி), offer refuge with sweet words knowing their own deceit, and measure out their love falsely (நின்றளந்தும் சளங்கொண்டிடும்). The Kural describes women who weigh the gain and then speak of their virtue (பயன்தூக்கிப் பண்புரைக்கும்) and tells a man to weigh them in turn and keep away. The song's measuring and the Kural's weighing name the same calculation behind the sweet words.

The Thiruppugazh describes lovemaking as falling into a sea of pleasure (இன்பவாரியில் விழுஞ் சிந்தையேன்) and asks how such a mind will ever reach the shore (கரைசேர்வேன்). In the Kural the woman says the sea of love surely exists (காமக் கடல்மன்னும் உண்டே) but there is no safe raft to cross it (ஏமப் புணைமன்னும் இல்). Both make desire a sea with no crossing; the Kural's lovesick woman wants to reach her lover, and the poet wants to get out of desire itself.

The Thiruppugazh pictures lovers entwined like anril birds until two hearts become one (அன்றில்போல் உளமிரண்டொன்றுமாய்), and asks to pass beyond the deeds those women bind him in. The Naladiyar quotes a paid woman who promised never to part, like the anril birds that never separate (புணர்பிரியா அன்றிலும்போல்), and then left. The anril, the bird of unbroken union, appears in both books inside the courtesan's embrace, and both poets look past it.

The Thiruppugazh lists the women's eyes as Kalakuta poison, cruel Death's form and Kama's arrows (கண் காளகூடம் கொடுங் கால்ருபம் பொரும் காமபாணம்), and asks whether his swinging senses will ever stop without saying 'Om namo Kanda'. The Kural's man asks whether the girl's look is Death, an eye or a doe (கூற்றமோ கண்ணோ பிணையோ). Both see death in a woman's eyes; the Kural says it in wonder, the song as a danger it wants a mantra against.

The Thiruppugazh asks not to be worn down by dog-like disputants (நாயொப்பவர்) who call good words evil (நற்சொலைத் தீதெனா) and argue against those who come to true austerity. The Naladiyar says that when the guileless explain virtue, the crooked do not hear it, just as the tanner's dog that chews leather cannot take the taste of milk-rice (குணுங்கர்நாய் பாற்சோற்றின் செவ்வி கொளல்தேற்றாது). Both use the dog for one who cannot receive good words.

The Thiruppugazh asks Murugan to end the nights of pleasure and give instead the bliss of silence and the dissolving of the mind (மவுனபஞ்சர மனோலயசுகம்). The Tirumanthiram teaches that mind and breath go together and that for those who rejoice within the abiding mind, the dissolving of mind (மனோலயம்) comes within it. The song asks for the state by name; the Tirumanthiram verse says how that dissolving is reached through the breath.

The Thiruppugazh describes women whose sword eyes, sharper than the vel, make war on young men's lives (இளைஞராவியை வளைந்தமர்செய் வாள்விழியர்) while their hearts hold deceit. The Kural's man says he never knew what Death was until now: it is a woman's grace with large eyes that make war (பேரமர்க் கட்டு). Both see the woman's eyes as a battle that takes a man's life; the song adds that the eyes serve a deceit aimed at his wealth.

The Thiruppugazh calls the body a hut filled with disease and evil (நோய்தீமை இட்டகுடில்) whose binding will come undone when Death's messenger comes, and asks Murugan to think of him before life is lost. The Kural asks whether the life, lodging in the body as a temporary shelter (உடம்பினுள் துச்சில் இருந்த உயிர்க்கு), has found no home of its own. Both make the body a poor lodging for life; the Kural leaves the question open, the song answers it with praise of the Lord.

The Thiruppugazh pictures the funeral: the bier lifted, the mourners calling, then plunging into the water (அலைநீரிற் புக்குமுழுகா) so that their long grief goes. The Tirumanthiram has the town wail, rename the man a corpse, burn him, then bathe in water and stop thinking of him (நீரினில் மூழ்கி நினைப்பொழிந்தார்). Both mark the ritual bath as the moment grief, and memory, are washed away; the song turns from it to ask for praise of the golden feet before that day.

The Thiruppugazh asks to see a lotus that neither water nor earth touches, spreading in length and breadth as a form of light (தாமரை படர்ந்தோடி நீளமகலஞ் சோதிவடிவான). The Tirumanthiram speaks of lotuses in bud which a spreading light opens (மொட்டலர் தாமரை ... சோதி விரிசுடர்). Both place the inner lotus and its light at the height of yogic vision; the Tirumanthiram verse is obscure, so the pairing rests on the image.
